policy_title: Ten-Year Plan for NHS Estates Investment
stated: Implement a ten-year plan to invest in hospitals and the primary care estate to end the scandal of crumbling roofs, dangerous concrete and life-expired buildings.

source.quote: Implement a ten-year plan to invest in hospitals and the primary care estate to end the scandal of crumbling roofs, dangerous concrete and life-expired buildings.

bearing_set.reason: Direct investment in NHS hospital and primary care infrastructure addresses capacity, safety, and access — materially affecting whether people can get treated when needed.

A decade-long capital investment programme in NHS estates constitutes a material public-spending commitment; whether it is funded from capital budgets or borrowed determines its effect on the debt path and the funded-vs-borrowed balance — a concrete fiscal mechanism, not a vague cost claim.

membership_note: Policy is a direct healthcare-infrastructure pledge with a clear fiscal footprint; O3 (delivery capacity) and O12 (public capital spending sustainability) both clear the non-negligible bar. No other fundamental is materially moved: labour-market effects (O4/O13) and distributional effects (O14) are too indirect and secondary.
